relevance_note: Single case report of an infant with a germline TNFAIP3 variant: "revealing a heterozygous mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene at chr6:138200458–138200459".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values were typed into a Python builder script, which mapped each span to the exact paper substring (the paper uses U+2005/U+2009 spaces) and failed on any non-match. Table 1 cells were read manually, not transcribed by script. Individuals: the single patient (label 'patient'), plus the father and mother, labelled from the Figure 4 legend, as tested relatives (Sanger: neither carried the variant). The patient's 'two half-brothers' ('had no similar medical history') were not given rows: they have no separate labels and no testing or specific clinical data. Table 1's bold marking of abnormal values is lost in the Markdown, so table abnormalities were judged against the printed reference ranges; borderline deviations (monocyte 16.6% vs 3-16%, eosinophil 0.9% vs 1-10%, RBC 4.10 vs a printed range of 4.3-14.2 x 10^12/L) and infection screening results were not recorded. Hepatomegaly/splenomegaly HPO candidates are my mapping of 'liver palpable 2.5 cm' and 'spleen palpable 1.5 cm below the costal margin'; the authors do not use those terms. Genital ulcers were checklisted 'excluded' from 'No abnormalities were detected in the anus or external genitalia' (one admission exam). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper says nothing about earlier reports. Inconsistencies noted in the paper: (1) Table 1 creatinine '3.03 mmol/L (0.8-5.3 mmol/L)' duplicates the BUN cell; (2) the RBC reference range repeats the WBC range; (3) the abstract says the patient was '1-month-old' while the case text says '48-day-old'; (4) the abstract says symptoms 'resolved completely with glucocorticoid monotherapy', but IVIG and antibiotics were given first and there were eight later hospitalisations with fever and raised inflammatory markers; (5) the abstract prints 'p. Leu626ValfsTer45' (with a space) and the Figure 4 legend 'NM_001270508.2c.1876_1877del' (no colon); the main-text form was used; (6) dsDNA was positive by ELISA but negative by IIF, and MPO/PR3 were positive while pANCA/cANCA were negative (different assays, recorded as given). No genome build is printed for the chr6 coordinates.
